In the pivotal setting of [[def-negligible-morphism-in-a-pivotal-category]], negligible morphisms are closed under addition, scalar multiplication, arbitrary composition on either side, and tensor product on the right by arbitrary morphisms. They are also closed under tensor product on the left, hence form a two-sided tensor ideal, under either of these sufficient hypotheses: the two pivotal traces agree on every endomorphism, or the category admits a braiding. In particular the conclusion applies to the planar Temperley–Lieb category and to the braided full tilting category used below. No factorization of an arbitrary tensor-product intertwiner is assumed.
[F1] Negligibility means $\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_Xgf)=0$ for all $g:Y\to X$ ([[def-negligible-morphism-in-a-pivotal-category]]).

Let $K$ be any field, $\delta\in K$, and let $0\le r\le n$ with $n-r$ even. Assume $r>0$ or $\delta\ne0$ or $n=r=0$. Put $A_n=\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\delta)$, use the right modules $W_{n,t}$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]], and put $D_{n,t}=W_{n,t}/\operatorname{rad}\phi_{n,t}$. There are $y,z:n\to r$ with $y\circ z^*=1_r$, and for $r>0$ both may be chosen as basis monic diagrams. There is an idempotent $e\in A_n$ with $eA_ne\cong A_r$ such that $M\mapsto Me$ is exact, sends $W_{n,t}$ to $W_{r,t}$, and sends $D_{n,t}$ to $D_{r,t}$, with value zero when $t>r$.

[F1] The right action is composition modulo diagrams of smaller propagation, and reflection reverses composition ([[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]], [[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-module-action-is-well-defined]], [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], [[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws]]).
[F2] The coefficient-of-identity forms are symmetric and satisfy $\phi(xa,w)=\phi(x,wa^*)$ ([[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-gram-form-is-invariant]]).
[F3] The nonzero form quotients $D_{n,t}$ are a complete pairwise nonisomorphic list of absolutely simple modules ([[cor-temperley-lieb-nonzero-cell-forms-classify-simple-modules]]).

[F2] The JW projector has “coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram,” is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by the elementary generators. Its corner is $p_a\mathrm{TL}_ap_a=\mathbb C(q)p_a$, and $\operatorname{Tr}_a(p_a)=[a+1]$ ([[lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-partial-trace-and-uniqueness]], Statement). For $a\ge1$, its defining recursion is $p_{a+1}=P_a-([a]/[a+1])P_aU_aP_a$ with $P_a=p_a\otimes1$. The initial values are $p_0=1_0$, $p_1=1_1$; the construction uses only the stated unit denominator quantum integers ([[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]], Definition).

[F3] A diagram is a noncrossing perfect matching. Stacking removes each closed cycle for a factor equal to the loop value and leaves the exterior matching; composition and horizontal juxtaposition extend bilinearly and form a strict monoidal category ([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], Definition; [[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws]], Statement).

[F4] The elementary cup-cap generators satisfy $U_i^2=\delta U_i$, $U_iU_{i+1}U_i=U_i$, $U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=U_{i+1}$, and distant commutation ([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]], Statement).

[F5] Every basis endomorphism diagram is a finite product of elementary generators; the product can be chosen without an intermediate closed cycle ([[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-generators-span]], Statement).

[F6] Closing a basis diagram with $c$ circles has value $\delta^c$, and this extends linearly. Closure is cyclic and factors through the stated cup/cap partial trace, with no division by the loop value ([[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]], Definition; [[lem-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-component-identities]], Statement).

[F7] “The homomorphism $\pi_n:P_n(R,\delta)\to\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ sending $u_i$ to $d_i$ is an isomorphism.” This holds for every commutative ring, without requiring the loop value to be nonzero or invertible ([[thm-temperley-lieb-presentation-isomorphism]], Statement).

[F3] Products $xy=x\circ y$ stack the left factor above the right factor; composition is associative and bilinear. ([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], [[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws]])

[F1] Diagram modules are free on noncrossing boundary pairings, composition removes each closed component with one factor $\delta$, and juxtaposition is strict monoidal ([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], [[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws]]).
[F2] Elementary cup-cap diagrams generate every endomorphism diagram ([[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-generators-span]]).

Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,
[F1] The recursion is $p_{r+1}=P_r-([r]/[r+1])P_rU_rP_r$, with $P_r=p_r\otimes1$ and the stated unit conditions ([[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]]).
[F2] The generators satisfy $U_i^2=\delta U_i$, $U_iU_{i+1}U_i=U_i$, and distant commutation ([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

[F4] Every basis endomorphism diagram is generated by the $U_i$; every nonidentity basis diagram has fewer than $n$ through strands ([[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-generators-span]], [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]).
[F5] The partial closure and unnormalized trace close the last strand and all strands, respectively ([[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]]).

[F6] For $n\ge1$, closing a last identity strand gives a factor $\delta$ and full closure factors through the partial trace. For $n\ge2$, closing $U_{n-1}$ on its last strand gives the straight identity on the remaining strands ([[lem-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-component-identities]]).
